* 1. execute
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: executor/execute
:FILE: src/graphden/executor/interface.clj
:LINE: 85
:MINS: 1.9
:END:

 *Start here.* ~execute~ is the public front door of the whole system. A caller hands it an execution *context*, a ~fn-id~ — the id of a row in the graph that *describes* a computation — and a map of free args. This ns is a thin, validating façade: it checks the args shape and delegates to the real machinery in ~compile-runtime~. Everything below is how that graph *description* becomes a value.

* 2. execute
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: executor/execute~2
:FILE: src/graphden/executor/compile_runtime.clj
:LINE: 1478
:MINS: 4.0
:END:

The dispatch heart of the hot path. It checks the cancellation / effect / execute-guard gates, pulls the *compiled registry* out of the context, looks up the closure for this ~fn-id~ (or throws fn-not-found), translates the caller's name-keyed args into the dual slot-id+name shape the compiled code expects, and finally calls ~(closure translated ctx)~. This is the moment *execute a fn* becomes *call a precompiled closure*.

:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: executor/create-context

:LINE: 406

Builds the ~ExecutionContext~ the previous step reads from. It carries the storage handle, the ~:base-fns~ impl registry (snapshotted from the global default), a lazily-filled ~:compiled-registry~ holder, the graph/deps caches, and the authz/effect seams. Because scoping (e.g. which branch) lives here, the *same* ~fn-id~ run in two contexts can resolve to different code — this is where that happens.

* 4. fill-graph-cache!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: executor/fill-graph-cache!
:FILE: src/graphden/executor/context.clj
:LINE: 359
:MINS: 2.7
:END:

How the graph cache is FILLED on a miss — and why the install is guarded. A write that commits while a loader is reading storage finds an empty cache (nothing to splice) and primes the post-write graph through its delta path; an unguarded loader would then put its pre-write read back over it, and readers would miss the fn they just created until the next write. So a loader takes the ctx's invalidation epoch BEFORE reading and installs under the invalidation lock only while that epoch still holds — a stale read is discarded, never published.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/executor/context.clj::(defn fill-graph-cache!][src/graphden/executor/context.clj:359]]
- same file :: [[file:executor.org::#executor/create-context][create-context]]

* 5. registry
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: executor/registry
:FILE: src/graphden/executor/compile_runtime.clj
:LINE: 926
:MINS: 3.0
:END:

Returns the ~{fn-id -> closure}~ map from the context holder. A warm holder is served straight back; if a full clear flagged it stale it is still served immediately while a background ~rebuild-optimistic!~ refreshes it (stale-while-revalidate — no reader ever blocks behind a ~50s cold compile). Only a genuinely COLD holder (boot, a divergent cold branch) compiles on demand under the invalidation lock, double- checked so concurrent callers coalesce onto one rebuild. This is the lazy *compile-once, reuse-forever* registry the executor runs against.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/executor/compile_runtime.clj::(defn registry][src/graphden/executor/compile_runtime.clj:926]]

Classifies each of a fn's root slots (via ~classify-slot~) into a ~:value~ / ~:free~ / ~:ref~ / ~:seq~ / ~:secret-value~ entry, memoised on the lookups. This classification is the pivot the code generator switches on next — the *shape* of every argument is decided here, once, at compile time rather than per execution.

* 11. compile-all
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: executor/compile-all
:FILE: src/graphden/executor/compile_eager.clj
:LINE: 1545
:MINS: 4.8
:END:

Topologically orders every impl-backed fn and compiles each in dependency order into ~{fn-id -> (fn [fa ctx])}~, cached process-wide by (graph-shape × base-fn set × ambient rich-types) — the rich-types component is load-bearing: ~produces-callable?~ HOF-wrap decisions depend on the swept ~:return-type~ entries, so callers under different types must not share a compile. Dependency order matters: by the time a parent compiles, its children's callables already exist to be wired in.

* 13. arg-builder
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: executor/arg-builder
:FILE: src/graphden/executor/compile_eager.clj
:LINE: 1031
:MINS: 8.8
:END:

Emits the per-binding ~(fn [fa ctx])~: ~:value~ becomes a constant, ~:free~ reads the slot-id (with a name fallback), ~:ref~ becomes a ~thunk~/delay that *defers* the child call, ~:seq~ becomes a lazy seq. This is the origin of graphden's laziness — refs are *wrapped, not evaluated*, so native Clojure ~if~/~and~/~or~ short-circuit for free without the executor knowing their names.

The read-side of laziness. Inside an impl this forces a ~thunk~ (calling it once), derefs an ~IDeref~/~delay~, or returns a plain value untouched. This is where a deferred ~:ref~ argument actually gets evaluated — at the moment, and only if, the impl reads it. Pair it with ~arg-builder~, which created the thunk.

* 17. call-with-cache
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: executor/call-with-cache
:FILE: src/graphden/executor/compile_eager.clj
:LINE: 704
:MINS: 3.2
:END:

Closes the loop. Child-callable invocations are memoised for the duration of one top-level ~execute~, keyed by ~[ref-id projected-free-args]~ in a per-call map (with a ~::nil~ sentinel and a size cap). This is how the lazy graph avoids recomputing the same sub-result and delivers a single cached value back up to the caller — the DRY principle, enforced at runtime.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/executor/compile_eager.clj::(defn- call-with-cache][src/graphden/executor/compile_eager.clj:704]]

* 18. map-fn
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: executor/map-fn
:FILE: resources/packages/core/hof/impls.clj
:LINE: 11
:MINS: 1.6
:END:

A HOF base-fn as the executor sees it: ~func~ arrives already ~hof-wrap~ped (the slot's type resolves to ~:fn~, so the executor hands over a callable, never a value) and the impl is one library call. The comment is the lesson — the seq is realised with ~doall~ INSIDE the execution scope, because a lazy seq escaping the effect-gate / trace / cancel bindings gets realised later, ungated and mislabeled. Streaming stays on the transducer arity.

- source :: [[file:../../../resources/packages/core/hof/impls.clj::(defbase map-fn ][resources/packages/core/hof/impls.clj:11]]

* 19. fix-fn
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: executor/fix-fn
:FILE: resources/packages/core/recursion/impls.clj
:LINE: 20
:MINS: 2.5
:END:

Recursion. A bare graph cycle through ~ref-fn-id~ is rejected at write time (twice — per binding, and at sync's topological sort), so a fn cannot name itself. ~:fix~ is the ONE door: ~step~ receives ~{:input … :self …}~ and re-enters through ~:self~, depth-capped by ~*max-recursion-depth*~. docs/RECURSION.md records the road not taken (lazy ref resolution) and why this combinator won.

- source :: [[file:../../../resources/packages/core/recursion/impls.clj::(defbase fix-fn][resources/packages/core/recursion/impls.clj:20]]

:PROPERTIES:

Which of a callback's free args are the per-element PARAMETERS and which are captured from the caller (docs/CLOSURE_CAPTURE.md). Resolution order: an authored ~:lambda-params~ on the fn-def (~[]~ = capture everything — handler chains), else the slot's structural ~[:fn {ARGS} RET]~ shape, accepted only when unambiguous. Everything ~hof-wrap~ does at call time was decided here at compile time.

* 21. build-ref-renames
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: executor/build-ref-renames
:FILE: src/graphden/executor/compile/renames.clj
:LINE: 1116

Renames, call-site half. When F renames a slot that its ref R still exposes under the original name (~{:as …}~, or a rename-view slot with ~source-slot-id~), the caller supplies the value under F's name and R reads its own — this builds the ~{R-name → F-name}~ translation applied to the free-arg map on the way into R. docs/adr/ADR-inherited-rename-surface.md: public names are the closest-chain rename, applied at the BOUNDARY; the walkers stay per-fid.

Renames, inherited half. An own rename slot whose source chain reaches OUTSIDE the root's slot set yields one alias per chain link, so an inner walker reading ~:branch-row~ finds the value the caller passed as ~:item~. Compile-time table, runtime copy — the worked example in the docstring is the one to trace by hand. This 1300-line namespace is the densest in the executor; these two entry points are its map.
